pages.text: $(l)1.9 million years ago.$() Kept fire, the Acheulean, shelter: everything so far, and the first things made to make other things.

$(l)Stone$() - a rock in hand, a hammerstone in the other, $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact): a $(l)flake$(), a $(l)chopper$(), a $(l)grinding stone$(), or the $(l)multi tool$() (8 chert, 10 basalt, 2 obsidian, or a chert hammerstone). Limestone will not take an edge: soft stone makes Lomekwian cores.

Everything habilis makes, and more. $(l)Two hands$(): a long branch and a rock - a $(l)club$(). Thatch and thatch - $(l)twine$(). A sharpened spear turned in a fire - right-click the fire with it four times, or hold it there - a $(l)fire-hardened spear$(). Four sticks and a hide - a $(l)knapping station$(). A log and a hide - a $(l)work station$().

At the $(l)knapping station$(): stone laid out on the mat, worked into a $(l)hand axe$() or a $(l)cleaver$() - the Acheulean. Good stone and practised hands make it finer: a tier from rough (4) to flawless (0). See The Language of Stone.

At the $(l)work station$(), the tool slot is the recipe: a log or long branch with a hand axe - $(l)workable branches$(); one with a cleaver - a $(l)shaft$(); two down the middle with a hammerstone - a $(l)club$(); a branch and any three rocks - $(l)building branches$(); a branch and three sticks - a $(l)cooking rack$().

Nine thatch, four twine in the slot - $(l)thatch blocks$(). Three hide over three thatch, ten twine - $(l)bedding$(). Three sticks along the bottom, a log in the middle, nothing in the slot - a $(l)fire pit$(). Thatch over a stick, three twine - a $(l)torch$(). A branch and a hammerstone side by side, ten twine - a $(l)digging stick$().

$(l)Fire$(): a fire pit, filled and lit with a drill - meat laid on it cooks. Two cooking racks with a branch across and a fire under it: ribs, chunks, marrow and the rest $(l)hung to cook$(). Blueprints ($(k:hominin_evolution.build)): a small hut, then a thatch tent.

$(l)An erectus band does what you do.$() They cut grass for thatch and hunt grazers for hides when the band is short, twist twine, and make thatch bedding at the work station - and sleep on a bed of their own rather than a nest. Spare thatch, twine and hides go in heaps by the work station for whoever is making something. They make clubs, cleavers and fire-hardened spears for themselves, too.
